title: Viral Nucleoprotein-Induced Microtubule Disruption: A Novel Pathogenic Strategy
content: Viruses, as obligate parasites, hijack and modify the host cell’s machinery to complete their life cycle. Most viruses exploit the cytoskeletal network, using it for intracellular transport to replication and assembly sites or to generate forces for viral egress [1-3]. Herpesviruses, such as varicella-zoster and HSV-1, as well as the rabies virus, exploit the cytoskeleton and neuronal transport to travel bidirectionally along axons, enabling efficient infection of the peripheral nervous system [4-5]. Furthermore, the Zika virus disrupts actin filament dynamics, enhancing viral infection [6]. Despite the cytoskeleton’s critical role in viral infection, the key cellular factors and molecular mechanisms underlying these processes remain largely unknown. Understanding these interactions is crucial for developing new treatments that target host proteins playing essential proviral roles in virus biology.
